faq.title: Automatic speech recognition FAQ
faq.description: Common planning questions for production ASR systems.

items.question: What is automatic speech recognition?
items.answer: Automatic speech recognition is the process of converting spoken audio into text. In production, it usually includes audio normalization, language handling, timestamps, speaker diarization, confidence scoring, review, and export workflows.

items.question: Is ASR the same as speech-to-text?
items.answer: Speech-to-text is the core output. ASR is often used for the broader recognition system that produces and manages that output, including timing, speakers, vocabulary, confidence, and downstream formatting.

items.question: How should I evaluate ASR accuracy?
items.answer: Use representative audio samples, measure word error rate, inspect speaker labels, test domain vocabulary, and record how much human review time is needed to make transcripts usable.

items.question: Do I need speaker diarization?
items.answer: Use diarization when audio includes multiple people and the transcript must show who spoke when. It is important for meetings, interviews, panels, calls, and compliance review.

items.question: What makes ASR hard in real workflows?
items.answer: Noise, accents, overlapping speakers, domain-specific terms, code-switching, privacy requirements, and latency expectations often matter as much as model accuracy.

faq.tip: Start with a small audio benchmark set before committing to a vendor, model, or deployment path.
